about: Every current doc route with a PROPOSED docs-graph placement. The docs graph spec is not decided; nothing here moves anything, and doc-routes.test.mjs fails when a current route has no row, a row names a route that no longer exists, or a row breaks the placement rules below.

Rows: one per built-in topic (`astryx docs <topic>`) and per section key (`astryx docs <topic> <key>`); typed descriptors take one row per provider and kind, with `count` and the ids in doc-routes.ids.json under the row id. Placeholders <id> expand per id. Per-item rows would repeat one decision per group hundreds of times (704 templates alone).

placement: keep-flat (the route stays where it is), namespace:<path> (the doc becomes <path> in the graph), or generated:<provider>/<kind> (the unorganized bucket for typed descriptors that author no placement). Anything but keep-flat carries a one-line evidence note, and a namespace must be decided `create` under namespaces.
aliasNeeded: true when the proposal leaves the old CLI route or docsite URL without its content unless an alias keeps it resolving. Sections move with their topic.

oldDocsiteUrl: the public docsite URL (paths on astryx.atmeta.com). Topic and section URLs are checked; section anchors are the docsite outline ids (slugged titles). docsiteExceptions on descriptor rows were measured on 2026-09-24 from a canary data build of apps/docsite and are not rechecked by the test; production documents the latest published core, so a newer component has no page until release.

namespaces.name: cli
namespaces.evidence: cli-integrations documents the CLI's integration surface (see its row), and the NamespaceDoc contract's own example is a 'cli' namespace for commands, APIs and integration authoring.
namespaces.note: `astryx docs cli` is the namespace's first reader: every doc whose namespace is cli/commands or cli/api, one section each. /docs/cli is still the @astryxdesign/cli package page on the docsite; the namespace page must take that URL before the docsite publishes it. Considered and left out: authoring, whose section docs declare namespace 'authoring', a sibling of 'cli' in the SchemaDoc contract.

namespaces.name: foundations
namespaces.evidence: Only the docsite's 'foundations' category label groups color, elevation, icons, illustrations, motion, shape, spacing, tokens and typography. The docsite serves each flat at /docs/<topic>, and icons and illustrations are not token pages.

namespaces.name: styling
namespaces.evidence: styling-libraries is linked from styling and from theme; only the hyphen suggests styling/libraries.

namespaces.name: theme
namespaces.evidence: No topic is a child of theme: theme descriptors and theme command docs are typed descriptors (generated bucket), and theme's 17 sections stay with it.

namespaces.name: migration
namespaces.evidence: migration is one guide with no child topics; the draft shadcn-compatibility doc is not a route, and version upgrades are the upgrade command doc.

namespaces.name: tokens
namespaces.evidence: The six token-category pages pull their tables from tokens by token reference; the only other tie is the tokenCategory label. Nothing authored nests them.

rows.evidence: No component doc authors a docs-graph placement.
rows.rationale: Unplaced typed descriptors go to their provider's generated bucket, not a guessed hierarchy; group and category fields are labels. The ids include the 10 core docs that `component <Name>` reads but `component --list` omits. No alias: `astryx component <id>` and /components/<id> are not docs-graph routes, and nothing here moves them.

rows.evidence: No doc of its own: `component <id>` resolves into another component doc, as a member of its components list or as the name the doc declares (NavMenu declares NavHeadingMenu).
rows.rationale: Neither `component --list` nor the compiler inputs list these names, yet each reads by name and has its own docsite page. The docs graph keeps one identity per doc file, so each name needs an alias to its parent doc.

rows.evidence: No hook doc authors a docs-graph placement.
rows.rationale: Unplaced typed descriptors go to their provider's generated bucket. The docsite serves hooks under /components/, next to components. No alias: neither route is a docs-graph route.

rows.evidence: No template doc authors a docs-graph placement; its category (for example 'Dashboard - Analytics') is a label.
rows.rationale: Unplaced typed descriptors go to their provider's generated bucket. Discovery reports built-in templates as @astryxdesign/core (the `template --list` package field) although the files ship in @astryxdesign/cli, and the provider follows discovery. /templates/<id> redirects to this canonical preview URL.

rows.evidence: No block doc authors a docs-graph placement; its directory and category are not placements.
rows.rationale: Unplaced typed descriptors go to their provider's generated bucket. The docsite renders blocks inside component pages as showcases and examples; no block has a URL of its own. Provider follows discovery, as for pages.

docsiteExceptions.chocolate: Not a docsite dependency: /themes?theme=chocolate shows Neutral without a message.

rows.evidence: No theme descriptor authors a docs-graph placement.
rows.rationale: Unplaced typed descriptors go to their provider's generated bucket. No read-only single-theme route exists: `astryx theme list` prints every descriptor, and `theme add <id>`, which writes files, is the only command that takes the slug.

rows.evidence: No command doc authors a docs-graph placement.
rows.rationale: Each CommandDoc builds its command's --help, and is also read as the section commands-<name> of `astryx docs cli` (see those rows): every command doc declares namespace cli/commands.

rows.evidence: No function doc authors a docs-graph placement.
rows.rationale: API reference for @astryxdesign/cli/api, read as the section api-<name> of `astryx docs cli` (see those rows): every function doc declares namespace cli/api. A wrapping command's --help also reuses its parameter descriptions.

rows.evidence: No schema doc authors a docs-graph placement.
